A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the water-soluble complexes bearing the DAPTA ligand exhibit the best phototoxic response in cancer cells, and the nature of the photoactivated cytotoxicity is likely due to a combination of CO release, 1O2 production, and the release of the photoproduct.

the water-soluble complexes bearing THP or DAPTA are photoactivated in vitro anticancer agents, and the complex bearing DAPTA and phenanthroline is the most promising candidate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the water-soluble phosphine ligands PTA, THP, and DAPTA are useful for the synthesis of rhenium(I) complexes that exhibit triplet-based luminessence and undergo photosubstitution.
the water-solubility of the phosphine ligand has a dramatic effect on the photochemical and photobiological properties of these compounds.
rhenium(I) tricarbonyl compounds bearing water-soluble phosphines are promising candidates for the development of new photoactivated anticancer drugs.
